pronouns.text: Thornwick green, under a hood, at the sweet stall. She raises a toffee apple to you like a toast, and waits to see what you'll do.
pronouns.say: He tells you something useful about Thornwick's spring exams. You tell him which Lumenhold porter sleeps through the ten o'clock bell, and regret it on the walk home.

absentFriend.text: Grisk takes this month's payment with a bow. "And do give my regards to Ilse," he adds. "Such a good friend to you. It would be a pity if she heard about our little friendship from anyone but you." He says it like a remark about the weather.
absentFriend.say: You tell Ilse that evening, all of it. She is quiet, then angry, though not at you. "He said that? Pay him off and never go near him again." Grisk, next month, seems a little less pleased with himself.

monthlyRefund.say: He tears the square out and folds it into his waistcoat pocket, next to his heart, if goblins keep them there. The envelope goes back in your purse. You can feel the folded paper all the way back up the hill.

noonOffice.text: After hours the counting house is yours again: empty desks, the smell of ink, and at high water the tide coming right in under the floor, slapping the piles. The night porter is lighting his lantern for his round of the moorings. He's been doing it since you were small enough to carry it.
